system_description.narrative_title: Energy markets roiled by Iran tensions and hurricane disruptions
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative links escalating Iran-related maritime attacks, sanctions and military incidents with concurrent hurricane disruptions in the Gulf, producing pronounced volatility across oil, gas, shipping and financial markets. Described as an open system, this energy–security–transportation complex continuously absorbs exogenous shocks (attacks, sanctions, storms, political statements), exchanges information, capital and physical flows with adjacent systems (financial markets, shipping networks, weather/climate), and generates feedbacks — price swings, route changes, production shut-ins and policy responses — that in turn alter actor behaviour and future risks.
system_description.scope: Crude oil and refined fuel production, Gulf of Mexico and Middle East export infrastructure, tankers and key chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz), shipping routes and maritime security, oil majors/traders/refiners, sanctions and military actions, weather-driven production disruptions, commodity price formation and futures trading, political statements and election-timing decisions affecting military policy.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic-energy system (international security, global trade, and financial markets)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and commodity trading
Energy transition and critical minerals supply chains

variables.name: Crude oil production rate
variables.description: The volumetric rate at which crude oil is being produced and brought to market per unit time across the system.

variables.name: Refined fuel production rate
variables.description: The rate at which refineries convert crude into finished transport fuels and other refined products per unit time.

variables.name: Offshore operational capacity
variables.description: The available operational capacity of offshore extraction and processing facilities expressed as usable fraction or volume.

variables.name: Tanker operational availability
variables.description: The proportion of merchant tanker fleet capacity that is available and deployable for commercial oil and fuel transport.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of hostile or disruptive incidents affecting maritime commerce (attacks, interdictions, boardings) per unit time.

variables.name: Chokepoint transit rate
variables.description: The number of commercial transits through critical maritime chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Shipping route diversion extent
variables.description: The average additional distance or time per voyage caused by route deviations from normal passages.

variables.name: Maritime insurance premium level
variables.description: The average cost of insurance and war-risk premia for maritime transport expressed as a price or percentage.

variables.name: Export infrastructure disruption level
variables.description: The aggregate degree to which export terminals, pipelines and loading facilities are impaired or offline.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: The share of refinery processing capacity that is actively operating and processing feedstock at a given time.

variables.name: Fuel inventory days of supply
variables.description: The amount of refined fuel stocks expressed in days of forward demand coverage at current consumption rates.

variables.name: Oil commodity price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for crude oil benchmarks measured in currency per unit of volume.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude of short-to-medium term fluctuations in commodity prices, measured by realized or implied volatility.

variables.name: Futures market liquidity
variables.description: The depth and ease of transacting in commodity futures and derivatives, proxied by bid-ask spreads and available open interest.

variables.name: Political and policy uncertainty level
variables.description: The perceived uncertainty about government actions (sanctions, military measures, trade restrictions) affecting the energy-transport system.

variables.name: Weather disruption severity
variables.description: The intensity and extent of weather events (storms, hurricanes) that disrupt production, shipping and onshore infrastructure.

catalysts.title: U.S. midterm elections (Nov 3, 2026)
catalysts.description: Scheduled U.S. midterm election day that could change policy posture toward Iran and energy-market risk premia.
catalysts.rationale: Trump says no attack before midterms; election can alter U.S. Iran policy and market risk premia (headlines 10/09-10/11).

catalysts.title: Sustained Iranian tanker attacks and Hormuz blockade threats
catalysts.description: Ongoing Iranian attacks on tankers and vows to block alternate Hormuz routes that maintain shipping risk and rerouting.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines report 'Iran attacks tankers', 'Attack risks rise' and falling Hormuz transits, driving continued maritime disruption (10/09-10/11).

catalysts.title: U.S. Treasury sanctions on Iran 'shadow fleet' enforcement
catalysts.description: Sanctions and enforcement actions targeting 17 tankers will constrain flagged vessels and shift commercial shipping behavior.
catalysts.rationale: Treasury sanctions 17 tankers and fresh sanctions reported; enforcement will reduce available tonnage and raise risk premia (10/09).

catalysts.title: Post-Isaias Gulf production and refinery shutdowns
catalysts.description: Ongoing shutdowns and staggered restarts of Gulf of Mexico platforms and refineries following Hurricane Isaias landfall.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Isaias made landfall, killed people, and disrupted US oil/gas production; companies curbed Gulf output (10/10-10/11).

catalysts.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens toward Mexico (Category 4)
catalysts.description: Rapid intensification of Hurricane Simon threatens Mexican Pacific coast, risking production outages and coastal infrastructure impacts.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note Hurricane Simon rapidly strengthened to Category 4 and threatens Mexican coast, implying near-term production/shipping risk (10/09-10/11).

catalysts.title: El Niño set to intensify through Feb 2027
catalysts.description: UN warns El Niño will intensify and persist to February 2027, raising probability of extreme weather disrupting energy supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: UN weather body says El Niño will intensify and last until Feb 2027, increasing weather-driven disruptions (10/09).

catalysts.title: Venezuela aims to sign 105 oil contracts by end of year
catalysts.description: PDVSA plans contract signings by year-end that could incrementally raise Venezuelan output and influence market supply expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Venezuela looking to sign 105 oil contracts by end of year — could lift supply expectations (10/09).

catalysts.title: Sustained diversion of commercial traffic away from Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Carriers continue to avoid Hormuz, lowering transit counts and lengthening voyages as attacks and risk premiums persist.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines report lowest Hormuz transits, captains paid steep fees, and carriers steering clear, implying sustained diversion impacts (10/09).

catalysts.title: Increased military interdictions and strikes in Gulf of Oman
catalysts.description: Recent U.S. strikes and interdictions of commercial vessels in Gulf of Oman risk further military-maritme escalations affecting shipping safety.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: US hits commercial tanker and disabled vessel attempting to run Iran blockade, raising risk of further military actions (10/11).
